doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Teaching online with movement and the 'walking through cheese' exercise
summary: Baron is teaching more students online with visualization and mindful breathing, and plans to try the walking-through-cheese exercise remotely.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well I’m about as crazy as everybody else I think. You know it’s a big mood swing roller coaster ride we’ve got going here. But try to practice, and I continue teaching, which is good. I’m getting more and more students to, you know, do it on the internet. And I’m pleased to say you know I use, let’s see, unorthodox teaching methods let’s say, with movement with visualization, breathing, mindful breathing and meditation and stuff. And it’s actually working. I’m pretty happy to say that.

I’m glad you said that because I went back and I was reading your interview and you had described at that time some of the things you did when a person came to your apartment for a lesson. And having them move around the space and sort of resistance, and these very interesting ideas. And I was thinking how would you do that?
Yeah, well are you talking about the “walking through cheese” one?

Yeah. Man, you can make a kid — an hour of walking through cheese is amazing, and I haven’t tried the walking through cheese yet, because I’d like to be moving when I’m doing it and I would — well, when I get my new computer I probably won’t need the earphones as much, but maybe I will, or I’ll get some speakers or something. But yeah, that could be a challenge but I’m going to give it a shot. I have a new trumpet student that I want to try that with. You know ‘cause it’s like we’ve got to make hay while the sun is shining any way we can.
